transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Time: 15:30-16:28 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Emily Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Jared Morris (AtlasPay Head of ML), Priya Gupta (Platform Eng), Sam Ortega (PM)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to agree on success criteria / acceptance tests for a 2-week POC. Discussed workloads (chat assistant + embedding batch), target QPS/latency, correctness thresholds, reporting format, and timeline. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Workload sizing: expected QPS, average tokens, concurrency
- Benchmarks: what to measure (p95 latency, p50, throughput, error rate, cost estimate)
- Success criteria: go/no-go thresholds for latency and quality (human-eval pass rate)
- Reporting: CSV + dashboard + raw logs, signoff process
- Timeline: staging setup, benchmark window, final report and signoff

Transcript:
00:00 Emily Chen: okay thanks everyone for joining. um quick intros, i'm emily, AE on the deal. Marcus is our se who will run the bench and the tech part.
00:06 Marcus Li: hey all, hi Jared, Priya, Sam. good to meet you. we'll go through what we need for the poc and propose acceptance tests.
00:15 Jared Morris: thanks. we are trying to validate that Redwood can handle our chat assistant workflow at scale while meeting latency & quality SLAs and also verify embeddings batch throughput for nightly jobs.
00:28 Emily Chen: great; can you give quick numbers for traffic? what are current RPS and typical tokens per request?
00:32 Priya Gupta: yeah so in prod we peak around 100 rps, sustained 60 rps. average user message ~40 tokens, reply average ~80 tokens, so call it ~120 tokens per request. concurrency around 50 on average.
00:45 Marcus Li: perfect that's helpful. for sizing we usually validate two buckets: interactive chat (low latency) and batch embeddings (throughput). for chat we'll run a steady state at 60 rps and a burst test to 120 rps to simulate peak.
00:58 Sam Ortega: what's acceptable latency for you? we prefer <300ms p95 but i think for us anything above 400ms feels slow.
01:06 Jared Morris: yeah our internal SLO is 250ms p95 for single-turn assistant, but we're willing to accept slightly higher during POC.
01:12 Marcus Li: okay proposed acceptance for chat: p95 <= 250ms for <=256-token combined context + response on dedicated capacity for 60 rps sustained. go/no-go if p95 > 400ms or error rate > 1%.
01:27 Emily Chen: agreed, we should also include throughput baseline: sustain 60 rps with p99 errors < 1% and tokens/s reported. we'll also provide cost estimate per 1M tokens for the tested config.
01:38 Priya Gupta: what about quality? latency is one thing, but correctness is crucial. we'll need a quantitative eval against our golden set.
01:45 Marcus Li: yes, acceptance test will include a golden prompt set (you mentioned 200 examples). we'll run automated checks: exact match where applicable and a semantic-match pass rate judged by a similarity threshold plus a small human review sample. proposed: automated pass >= 90% and human adjudicated agreement >= 85%. go/no-go if automated pass < 80% or human agreement < 70%.
02:05 Jared Morris: sounds reasonable. how do you measure semantic match? cosine on embeddings or some LLM-based rubric?
02:12 Marcus Li: we provide both: a vector-similarity based metric (cosine on sentence-transformer embeddings) with threshold you define, plus our optional LLM-rubric scorer that compares answers to golden responses. we'll output both in the report.
02:26 Sam Ortega: what about streaming / partial replies? some of our flows use streaming and we care about time-to-first-token.
02:33 Marcus Li: good call. we'll include TTF (time-to-first-token) and p50, p95 for TTF separately. acceptance for TTF p95 < 120ms for streaming-enabled paths.
02:45 Emily Chen: for batch embeddings, what do you run nightly? size & deadline?
02:50 Priya Gupta: nightly job is ~1.5M texts, currently runs for 6 hours on our infra. we'd like to reduce that to <2 hours ideally.
02:58 Marcus Li: we'll run a scaled batch test on a representative sample and extrapolate tokens per second. acceptance: full run estimated <2.5 hours on designated hardware (we'll propose a Dedicated GPU profile). go/no-go if extrapolated run >4 hours or error rate for embeddings >0.5%.
03:13 Jared Morris: what hardware are you planning for the POC? A100? T4?
03:18 Marcus Li: for initial tests we'll offer a couple of variants: A10/A100 for dedicated, also a quantized variant on T4 for cost comparison. we'll note model variant and quantization in every report.
03:29 Emily Chen: reporting format: we'll produce a csv with per-request latency, TTF, tokens in/out, error flags, model version, host id, plus a dashboard with aggregated p50/p95/p99 and throughput curves. raw logs can be shared via s3 link.
03:42 Priya Gupta: we need auditability: timestamps, request ids, and ability to map to our eval ids.
03:48 Marcus Li: yes we'll include request_id mapping and a header row that includes your eval id that you pass in.
03:55 Sam Ortega: timeline? how long for POC?
04:00 Emily Chen: proposed 2-week POC: week 0 (setup): staging onboarding, network/VPC peering or private endpoint, share security docs. week 1: run initial functional tests and small-scale correctness passes. week 2: full benchmarks + run acceptance tests, generate report and review. final signoff within 3 business days after report.
04:22 Jared Morris: that timeline is fine, we may push the benchmark window to next week if you can provide the harness quickly.
04:29 Emily Chen: we'll aim to share harness & runbook by 2025-02-14. can you confirm eval dataset by the same date?
04:36 Priya Gupta: yes we'll get the 200-sample eval set and traffic histograms by 2025-02-14.
04:41 Marcus Li: one minor note on measurement noise: we'll re-run each scenario 3 times and report median across runs, and we'll provide raw per-run files so you can inspect outliers.
04:54 Jared Morris: security questions: SOC2 / ISO? we need KMS for keys, and audit logs.
05:00 Emily Chen: Redwood has SOC2, we have ISO docs as well. for private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations and will provide audit log options. we'll share the security packet separately.
05:10 Priya Gupta: any dependencies on our side for the benchmark? VPC peering or staging keys?
05:15 Emily Chen: we need either a staging VPC endpoint or temporary IAM creds to hit the staging endpoint. se will send a checklist.
05:22 Marcus Li: noted. also need example payload shape and your auth header so we can replicate exactly.
05:28 Sam Ortega: final signoff process? who signs?
05:32 Jared Morris: i'll be the technical acceptor but product will do a final review. we'll sign off in writing by email within 3 business days if thresholds met.
05:40 Emily Chen: great. recap of acceptance thresholds (read back): for chat: p95 <= 250ms for <=256 tokens at 60 rps, go/no-go if p95 > 400ms or errors >1%. TTF p95 < 120ms. Quality automated pass >=90% with human agreement >=85% (fail if automated <80% or human <70%). Batch embeddings: full job <2.5 hours extrapolated (fail if >4 hours) and embedding error rate <0.5%. report delivered as csv + dashboard + raw logs, signoff within 3 business days.
06:20 Jared Morris: that's what we need. sounds good.
06:23 Emily Chen: ok we will send the runbook + schedule the benchmark window for 2025-02-19 09:00-12:00 PT.
06:29 Priya Gupta: confirmed tentative. we'll sync internally and confirm by 2025-02-14.
06:34 Emily Chen: excellent. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with security docs and the harness.
06:38 Jared Morris: thanks, bye.
06:40 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: some short timestamps are approximated, and there may be minor mis-hearings (e.g., K V cache transcribed inconsistently).
